title: Minimum set cover

problem.name: Minimum set cover
problem.statement_latex:
Given a universe $U$, $|U|=n$, and an explicit family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^U$, $|\mathcal F|=m$, minimize $|\mathcal C|$ subject to $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F$ and $\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal C}S=U$. Typical interpretations select facilities, tests, or resources that jointly cover all requirements.
The quantum bound counts QRAM time, the subset algorithms count classical RAM operations, and the CNF-based bounds count bit operations on explicit inputs.
problem.statement_text: Given a universe $U$, $|U|=n$, and an explicit family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^U$, $|\mathcal F|=m$, minimize $|\mathcal C|$ subject to $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F$ and $\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal C}S=U$. Typical interpretations select facilities, tests, or resources that jointly cover all requirements. The quantum bound counts QRAM time, the subset algorithms count classical RAM operations, and the CNF-based bounds count bit operations on explicit inputs.

quantum.details_latex: Polynomial factors include the explicit family size $m$. The method combines subset preprocessing with recursive quantum minimum finding and assumes coherent table access. Its exponential parameter is universe size $n$, allowing the family to be larger than a linear number of sets.

classical.headline_latex: $O^*(\min\{2^n,2^m\})$, subset dynamic programming or family enumeration.
classical.headline_text: $O^*(\min\{2^n,2^m\})$, subset dynamic programming or family enumeration.
classical.details_latex: For $m=\Theta(n)$, a stronger bound is $O_\epsilon(2^{\epsilon n}\operatorname{poly}(n,m))$ for every fixed $\epsilon>0$, from long-clause shortening and fixed-width counting. Selection variables, element-cover clauses and a linear-size cardinality circuit give $O(n)$ variables and clauses in this regime. If element frequency is fixed and $m=O(n)$, the encoding has fixed width and linear size, giving $\operatorname{poly}(n,m)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time. The unrestricted-family comparison and these linear-family regimes use different relations between $n$ and $m$.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant in the unrestricted-family, universe-size comparison, from amplitude amplification. For a linear-size explicit family, the subexponential classical bound is asymptotically smaller.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum upper bound is rigorous in QRAM. The broader Set Cover Conjecture concerns specified universe-size and family-size regimes; the linear-family subexponential bound must be included when selecting that comparison.

hardware.description_latex:
Polynomially many active subset and objective qubits accompany exponentially large coherent preprocessing memory. The storage and long nested searches make useful instances a fault-tolerant target.
{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the explicit-family comparison used $O^*(\min\{2^n,2^m\})$ classically and $O^*(1.7274^n)$ quantumly, including the linear-family regime now covered by the subexponential bound.]\par}
